doc.title: Eddie Marshall interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

title: San Francisco embraces him; Yoshi's and the jazz festival
summary: He describes a supportive community of friends and musicians, with Yoshi's and the year-round jazz festival keeping jazz alive.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Well the San Francisco community seems to have embraced you as an institution.

Oh yeah. It’s either that or I should be institutionalized. No I mean it’s like a mutual love affair. You know it’s a situation where like I moved out here with no immediate family here, but I have a great family here, a family of friends and musicians that I have met here who really support me and jazz music in general. They really do. A lot of these club owners, they make a strong effort to keep jazz in San Francisco. There’s no real major jazz club in San Francisco. You know there’s no Keystone anymore. The major jazz club in this area is Yoshi’s, which is a very fine club. They keep the banner waving by bringing acts from all over the world into Yoshi’s. But we don’t have — we have the alternative, which is a pretty good alternative, is our year round San Francisco Jazz Festival at [inaudible], which nobody gave a prayer to when it first — I mean this thing, a jazz festival all year round in a city of less than 700,000 people. But it’s working. He’s a busy person.
